summary: P95/P99 latency spikes and occasional request timeouts after continuous-batching change
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (notably LexiHealth) are reporting intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional 504 request timeouts starting after the 2026-02-25 scheduler rollout. Spikes are visible in token-level and request-level latency graphs and correlate with increased batch formation time in the serving runtime.

Impact:
- Multiple customers observing elevated p95/p99 (2-10x baseline) during short-sequence workloads.
- A subset of requests hit 30s client-side timeouts and retry, increasing downstream load.
- Customer-facing features (search summarization, chat) degraded for enterprise customers in us-east.

Environment:
- prod cluster: us-east primary, some reports from eu-west.
- serving-runtime: v2.4.1
- scheduler: v1.9.0 (rolled out 2026-02-25)
- continuous-batching: enabled with default window config

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run a steady stream (50-200 QPS) of short prompts (avg 10-30 tokens) to the hosted API pinned to redwood/gpt-3.5-small.
2) Observe request latency at p95/p99 using console or datadog dashboards for route/model.
3) Reproduce locally by enabling continuous-batching with the same scheduler config and short-sequence traffic pattern.

Logs / Evidence:
- Datadog dash: token/per-request latency spikes correlated to batch formation time (link redacted).
- Request traces show long time spent in batch queue before execution (~50-300ms outlier batches).
- Serving runtime logs: several "batch-evicting" traces aligned with scheduler decisions and timers.
- Error samples: intermittent 504s observed on gateway when downstream requeues exceed client timeout.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: scheduler change (v1.9.0) modified batch timer behavior leading to larger, less-predictable batch windows for short sequences.
- Confirmed correlation between rollout timestamp and initial spike start in global metrics.
- Canary tests where max_batch_wait_ms was reduced to 8ms showed immediate reduction in p99 but increased overall token cost due to smaller batches.
- Some customers see spikes only when request mix includes many short, low-token requests; long requests unaffected.
- Noted a fallback path where kernel selection for certain quantized model variants sometimes introduces additional scheduling latency - investigating with runtime team.

Mitigation / Next steps:
- Immediate: enable targeted canary rollback of scheduler change for affected us-east pools while engineering prepares a patch (ENG-rollback planned).
- Short-term: tune max_batch_wait_ms for affected fleets to 8-12ms as a temporary mitigation; communicate cost implications to customers.
- Medium-term: implement adaptive batch timer that is workload-aware (short-sequence vs long-sequence heuristics) and add metrics to detect pathological batch-formation delays.
- Engineering owner: Ravi Patel. SRE: Priya Nair. Runtime lead: Tomas Alvarez.

Resolution notes (ongoing):
- Rollback to scheduler v1.8.7 pinned on 2026-02-28 for 40% of us-east capacity; observed median/p95 improvement in canary. Full rollback scheduled if metrics continue to improve.
- PR created to add guardrails and a feature flag around new scheduler behavior: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/981.
- Follow-up: create a postmortem template entry and update Continuous Batching Runbook with new tuning knobs.
